html:
The Atacama Large Millimeter Array, ALMA, is a radio telescope of 66 antennas on the Chajnantor plateau in northern Chile, about 5,000 metres above sea level. It was inaugurated in 2013.

The Atacama Desert is one of the driest places on earth, with clear, steady skies, and since the 1960s European and American observatories have been built there. ALMA, run by Europe, North America and East Asia with Chile, studies cold gas and dust where stars and planets form. In 2019 it helped make the first image of a black hole.

Chile now hosts a large share of the world's big telescopes, with more being built. The same desert held the nitrate towns and the Chinchorro mummies.
